stops.note: meant 'Dwelling-Place-of-Lions Island', an old name for the island now called Sri Lanka
stops.meaning: an old name for the island of Sri Lanka

stops.note: Arab traders adopted the Sanskrit place name for the island
the old name entered English via Persian tales and travel writing
stops.meaning: an old poetic name for Ceylon

stops.note: coined by Horace Walpole from the fairy tale 'The Three Princes of Serendip', whose heroes made lucky discoveries by accident
stops.meaning: the faculty of making fortunate, unexpected discoveries

current_meaning: The occurrence of pleasant or valuable discoveries by accident; a fortunate, unplanned finding.
